actions.body: Existing research, such as the comprehensive survey in source-db145486024f469a and source-f955850b0fcf467a, indicates that while cognitive architectures (like SOAR or ACT-R) have long integrated self-monitoring through production rule consistency or symbolic trace checking, modern neural-based agents rely increasingly on externalized monitoring (e.g., meta-prompting, reflection loops). The literature suggests a gap: structural self-correction inside the core logic is often implicit or hard-coded rather than emergent. Source-bda2bc47c38c47a2 highlights that even comparative tables of these architectures often omit granular error-correction methodologies, treating 'self-correction' as a monolithic feature rather than a measurable process. Future work must differentiate between reactive correction (after failure) and proactive monitoring (during deliberation).
actions.lede: Cognitive architectures and AI agent designs exhibit shared evolutionary patterns and structural categorizations, yet the mechanisms for self-correction remain fragmented across the literature.
